raw_response:
*Sitting down, thinking it over...*

Well, my fields are only 5 mu — not big, but it's been my family's land for a long time. I've been doing wheat and corn on this same ground for more than thirty years, ever since my father handed it over. With 7 mouths in the house and the older boys working in the city now, the farming mostly falls on me and my wife, and the kids help when they're back. So I keep it simple. I do what worked last year, and what my neighbors are doing.

**For my wheat (winter wheat, October to June):**

I'll plant after I clear the corn in October, around the 10th if the weather is dry. I usually buy Jimai seed at the supply store — a few of us in the village use the same one, the agent recommended it years ago and it does fine. I save some seed too, but the bought seed comes up better.

For fertilizer, before planting I spread about one bag of compound (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu, that's roughly 50 kg. Then in the spring at jointing, when the wheat starts standing up, I topdress urea, about half a bag per mu — say 20 kg. My neighbor Old Wang puts on more, but I can't afford to throw money at it, and my yields are okay. If the wheat looks yellow I'll add a bit more, but usually it's fine.

I water three times if the weather is normal — once in winter to set the roots, once at jointing in spring, once at grain filling. The well costs money to run, so if it rains good I skip one. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see aphids near harvest I'll spray insecticide. I hire the combine at harvest, everyone does, no point cutting by hand anymore.

I usually get around 400-420 kg per mu. Last year was 410. That's what I plan for.

**For my corn (summer maize, June to September):**

Right after the wheat combine leaves the field — same day or next morning — I have to get the corn in. Window's only a few days. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has, costs about 50 yuan per mu but worth it. I don't till — I just drill the corn straight into the wheat stubble. Saves time and money.

Base fertilizer is one bag of compound per mu at planting, then in late July when the corn is at the big bell stage I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu. Corn likes nitrogen, but I've learned not to overdo it because then it falls over in storms.

Summer rains are usually enough — I water once or twice if July is dry, no more. Spray herbicide at planting, and if the corn borers come bad I spray once. Hire the combine again in late September.

Corn yields better than wheat for me — 450 kg per mu in a normal year, sometimes touch 500.

**About money and labor:**

Total for the year I'll spend maybe 4,500 yuan on inputs and machine hire across the 5 mu. That's not nothing for us, but the off-farm wages from the boys help cover it. My wife and I do most of the field work — call it 30-35 days of family labor across the year between the two crops. Only thing I hire is the combines and sometimes the rotary tiller before wheat planting.

I'm not trying to win any prizes. I just want both crops in, both crops harvested, enough grain for the family's flour and feed, and the rest sold to cover next year's inputs. That's how I've done it, and that's how I'll do it again.
